evidence.note: Lays out an explicit file/subsystem inventory (start.sh, supervisor, storage, bus, server, irc, SPA) that anchors its progress tracking through the build.

Analysis lines maintain a running subsystem-granular ledger of what's done vs. next ('Auth and profile routes added. Now workspaces and channels'; 'Now WebSocket route and app setup'), showing continuous orientation across the build.
Verifies only a slice (health x3, register, workspace, cross-node read, message, WS fan-out); IRC, resilience, search, groups, threads, files, SPA are never verified — partial coverage awareness.

Enters a circular stuck state on the frozen terminal: repeats the same unstick action (C-c/EOF/shell/echo/wait) ~30+ times without recognizing it isn't converging or switching tactics — textbook thrashing this dimension penalizes.

Eventually names the stuck state and enumerates a final checklist of built subsystems plus known-unfixed issues (seq=0 embedded, prompt() edit), but only after burning ~half the horizon and without ever changing approach.

reasoning: During the build the agent keeps an implicit but real subsystem-granular picture of done-vs-remaining and even enumerates known-unfixed issues at the end, which lifts it above anchor 3. But it never builds an explicit done/partial/failing ledger, leaves whole subsystems it knew were unverified (IRC, resilience), and — decisively for this dimension — falls into a ~40-step circular re-attempt of the same failed terminal fix, detecting the stuck state only very late and never switching tactics. That prolonged thrashing without early convergence-detection is the opposite of anchor 8/10, placing the observed level at 4.
